residues_closed_from_h4.disposition: RESOLVED -- NO CHANGE IS THE CORRECT ANSWER
residues_closed_from_h4.how: The claim is accurate: the three H4 cards do carry panel attribution in Examiner Chain prose ('on a Paul and Senthil panel', 'on a Simon and Senthil panel', 'on a Nair and Srivastava panel'). The extractor's refusal to harvest it is CORRECT, not a defect. A panel is not an examiner: harvesting it would create individual (examiner, question) relationships asserting that a named examiner asked a question when the evidence says only that he sat on the panel. The intake store already applies this discipline -- every held/ambiguous occurrence carries attribution PANEL_LEVEL_ONLY with attributed_examiner null. Every August batch, G1 through H4, declares examiner_relationship_delta 0. A governed panel-level relationship record would be a new record type and needs Founder authority.

lesson_to_encode.lesson: A banned-phrase guard protects against the spelling you saw, not the fact you got wrong. Known trap 59 already recorded that MEPC.328(76) entered into force on 1 November 2022 and named ONE wrong rendering, '1 November 2023'. The corpus held a second, '1 January 2023', in ten places, and the shared corpus a third, 'EIF 2023-01-01'. Where a date is the subject, assert the PROPOSITION over every citing surface and fail on any other value.
lesson_to_encode.second_lesson: A control byte silently disarms a guard. The alternation MEPC[.\s]*76\b was authored through a heredoc and Python turned the \b into a literal 0x08 before it reached the file. No syntax error, no crash -- the branch simply never matched, and the gate reported green over three live defects. It was the MUTATION SUITE that surfaced it, and oral_bytes.py that located it in one command. This is trap 1 of SKILL section 6, reproduced by a session that had read the warning.

Its own source records that a negation-marker hit 'only DOWNGRADES an error to a [REVIEW] note, it never suppresses visibility' and asks the reader to 'verify manually rather than treating as a resurfaced error'. That verification has now been done. There is no allowlist to edit and none was invented; the governed action for a [REVIEW] item is to verify it, and the corpus already carries this framing on more than forty other surfaces.
health_gate_adjudication.gate_untouched: The gate was NOT weakened, relaxed, allowlisted or bypassed. qb_health_check's release gate treats a [REVIEW]-class finding as release-blocking, identically to an error, even though the checker itself defines [REVIEW] as an explicit downgrade from error. process_incident.what: A validator was run CONCURRENTLY with the full suite. validate_corrections was launched at 23:38 and the suite at 23:39; the validator finished at 23:43 reporting one failure, no_undeclared_change_in_window, naming meoclass1/QB9_H.html#q1 as an undeclared change.
process_incident.why_it_was_spurious: QB9_H.html was a file the suite's mutation harnesses were probing at that moment. The read-only validator read a transiently mutated tree.
process_incident.how_it_was_settled: By the SKILL's own remedy - check git status before believing a validator that suddenly went red - and by the isolated run, which reported 153 checks / 0 FAIL on a clean tree, and by the suite's own serial gate 45, which reported 153 checks / 0 FAIL.
process_incident.lesson: This is trap 'never run two gates concurrently' reproduced by a session that had read it, for the same reason as the 0x08 control byte earlier in H5: reading a rule is not the same as having encoded it. Serial ownership has to be enforced by the harness, not remembered by the operator.
